item.title: Ngshiu family gives back to Lomary Raluve team with timely support
item.description: New Zealand Sevens representative Tone Ngshiu, together with his family and representatives from Nanuku Resort, rallied behind Lomary Secondary School's Under-18 Raluve team by donating training equipment and food supplies during the Vodafone Weet-Bix Raluve National Championship. item.content:encoded:
New Zealand Sevens representative Tone Ngshiu, together with his family and representatives from Nanuku Resort, rallied behind Lomary Secondary School's Under-18 Raluve team by donating training equipment and food supplies during the Vodafone Weet-Bix Raluve National Championship.

The presentation took place following the team's captain's run, with the donations aimed at supporting the players as they prepared for the knockout stages of the competition.

The gifts included training equipment and food items to help the players with their preparations and wellbeing throughout the tournament.

School officials thanked the Ngshiu family and Nanuku Resort for their generosity, saying the gesture lifted the players' spirits and reminded them that they had the support of the wider community.

They say the donation was about more than providing equipment and food—it gave the players confidence and showed them that their commitment and hard work are recognised beyond the rugby field.

The support came before Lomary's quarter-final clash against Bua Central College, with the team going on to defeat Bua Central 38-5 to book a place in the semi-finals.

School officials say acts of generosity such as this inspire young athletes to keep striving for excellence, knowing there are people willing to invest in their future.

item.title: Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Salove fight back to draw 1-1 with Savusavu
item.description: Mohammed Feroz , Nilufa Buksh · 09/08/2026 Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Meat Salove fought back from a goal down to hold Savusavu to a 1-1 draw in an entertaining Super Premier Division match on the second day of the Matuku Spares Vanua Levu Muslim IDC at Subrail Park.
item.content:encoded:
Mohammed Feroz , Nilufa Buksh · 09/08/2026

Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Meat Salove fought back from a goal down to hold Savusavu to a 1-1 draw in an entertaining Super Premier Division match on the second day of the Matuku Spares Vanua Levu Muslim IDC at Subrail Park.

Savusavu made a strong start and took a 1-0 lead into halftime after scoring in the opening spell.

Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Salove responded strongly after the break, applying sustained pressure and capitalising on a counter-attack to score the equaliser.

Both teams created chances to snatch the winner, but solid defending and impressive goalkeeping ensured the points were shared.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports after the match, Blue Ray and Tebara Supermarket Salove coach Sabid Ali praised his players for their performance and says the team is now focused on securing a place in the quarter-finals.

Ali says he urged his players to remain disciplined and continue putting pressure on their opponents.

He says his halftime message was simple, to score the equaliser after going into the break trailing by one goal.

Ali also thanked the supporters who travelled from Viti Levu and those who came to Subrail Park to support the tournament.

Meanwhile, defending champions Tasrif Khan Seaqaqa thrashed Korowiri 5-0 in the Super Premier Division, while Batinikama and Basoga played out a goalless draw in the Premier Division.

item.title: Rewa determined to make fans proud in Champions League opener today
item.description: Rewa FC is determined to give 100 percent and make their families and fans proud when they take on Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC in their OFC Men’s Champions League opener at 3pm today. Rewa FC player Setareki Hughes says the team is excited to play the tournament on home soil and has been preparing well for the challenge.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC is determined to give 100 percent and make their families and fans proud when they take on Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC in their OFC Men’s Champions League opener at 3pm today.

Rewa FC player Setareki Hughes says the team is excited to play the tournament on home soil and has been preparing well for the challenge.

Hughes says having eight players from the Pro League, along with players from other Pro League teams, has provided a major boost to the squad.

He says the players are looking forward to giving their best throughout the tournament.

He says Rewa FC expects all teams in their group, including Galaxy FC, Lae City and Tupapa Maraerenga, to provide a tough challenge.

Hughes says the teams have arrived well prepared and expects good matches during the tournament.

Rewa FC will face Galaxy FC at 3pm today at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

item.title: South Africa hold off Argentina 17-10 as Kolisi suffers injury
item.description: South Africa survived a late-scare by Argentina to hang on for a 17-10 win in Buenos Aires on the back of an inspirational performance from No.8 Cameron Hanekom. However, it came at a cost as inspirational captain Siya Kolisi was injured in the process.
item.content:encoded:
South Africa survived a late-scare by Argentina to hang on for a 17-10 win in Buenos Aires on the back of an inspirational performance from No.8 Cameron Hanekom.

However, it came at a cost as inspirational captain Siya Kolisi was injured in the process.

Down by seven a 50-22 with one minute remaining gave Argentina one last chance to level the game.

After 14 phases, the Pumas went wide where centre Matias Moroni had a chance to score in the corner but the high pass slipped through his hands into touch ending the game.

Earlier, a first half onslaught by Argentina left the Springboks fighting hard to stay in the Test.

The Pumas and Springboks traded penalties early before the home side landed the first blow through openside Benjamin Grondona running over untouched from 10 metres out following an offload in the tackle.

Argentina held a 10-3 lead for most of the half as a physical battle led to a stalemate despite the Pumas finding six line breaks.

The Pumas kick plan found plenty of success with attacking chips and cross field kicks leading to break opportunities, with wing Ignacio Mendy finding four in the first half.

As the second half wore on, the volume of kicks began to turn the territory advantage completely in South Africa’s favour while errors by the Pumas played into the Boks hands. A loose lineout by Argentina gave the Springboks an attacking entry into the 22 from which Esterhuizen was held up.

The injeciton of the Springboks bench helped lift the visitors, improving the scrum and maul and providing more power in the carry game.

A helter-skelter period of play and the continued kick heavy game plan gave South Africa the territory to get ahead on the scoreboard after forcing multiple goal line drop outs.

A kick in-behind by Handre Pollard turned into a collapsed maul turnover after they held up Argentina’s fullback Geronimo Prisciantelli.

A dominant scrum gave the Boks penalty advantage from which No.8 Cameron Hanekom dived over for a 17-10 lead.

They would hold on with a big defensive stand to finish the game, repelling the Argentineans repeatedly before the final pass went into touch.

Siya Kolisi confirmed in his post-match interview that he had a hamstring issue and will go for scans to determine the extent.

Kolisi is now in doubt for the Greatest Rivalry Tour by the All Blacks who will play the Sharks at 5am Wednesday.

item.title: Grammar will meet Ra High in Deans semifinal
item.description: Suva Grammar School will meet Ra High School in the Vodafone Super Deans semifinal next week after beating Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute 23-7 this evening. The boys from Nasese ran in four tries, while Alfred Cornish scored Ba Pro's lone try.
item.content:encoded:
Suva Grammar School will meet Ra High School in the Vodafone Super Deans semifinal next week after beating Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute 23-7 this evening.

The boys from Nasese ran in four tries, while Alfred Cornish scored Ba Pro's lone try.

The Grammar forwards dominated the collision area before spreading the ball wide.

Ba Pro was eventually able to score in the second half taking advantage of the one man advantage as the Grammer centre was still in the sin bin through their flanker who broke two tackles before sprinting over 30 metres to score under the sticks.

With the last quarterfinal now being played, the semifinal fixtures are now confirmed with Nasinu Secondary School to play Lelean Memorial School next week.

In the games earlier today at Garvey Park, Tavua, Ra High caused an upset when they edged defending champions Ratu Kadavulevu School 12-10, while Nasinu defeated Cuvu High School 28-26.

At the HFC Bank Stadium, Lelean thumped Ratu Navula 26-5 in the first quarterfinal.

item.title: Fijiana XV fall 55-12 to clinical Springbok Women
item.description: The Vodafone Fijiana XV went down 55-12 to a clinical Springbok women in their inaugral Ubuntu-Bula Trophy game at the HFC Bank Stadium this afternoon. There were moments of indiscipline for the Fijiana as they spent 20 minutes a player down after No. 8 Alfreda Fisher was yellow carded, which was later upgraded to red for diving in at the ruck and catching the opposing player on the head.
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fijiana XV went down 55-12 to a clinical Springbok women in their inaugral Ubuntu-Bula Trophy game at the HFC Bank Stadium this afternoon.

There were moments of indiscipline for the Fijiana as they spent 20 minutes a player down after No. 8 Alfreda Fisher was yellow carded, which was later upgraded to red for diving in at the ruck and catching the opposing player on the head.

The South Africans ran in 10 tries to the Fijiana's two tries from Adi Vani Buleki and Varanisese Qoro.

Captain Kelera Lomani says their collision let them down today.

Lomani says they will go back and review the footage to see what they can improve on before next week's game.

She also thanked the fans that came out to support them, as well for the love and support they have for the Fijiana team.

The Springbok women led 27-7 at the break.

The two sides will face off again next week at Churchill Park, Lautoka for their second Test.
